Wind Protection: The Comfort Game-Changer

Wind noise and buffeting are the biggest sources of fatigue on long motorcycle tours. At 70mph, the wind force on your body is equivalent to holding a 30kg weight at arm's length. A properly chosen windscreen dramatically reduces this force, making hundred-mile motorway sections relaxing rather than exhausting.

How Windscreens Work

A windscreen redirects airflow over and around the rider. The ideal screen creates a pocket of still air that protects your helmet and upper body. If the screen is too short, the redirected airflow hits you at chest or helmet height, creating more turbulence than no screen at all. If it is too tall, you may look through it, which reduces visibility in rain.

Choosing the Right Height

  • Look over, not through — The screen top should be at chin or nose height when in the riding position. This directs airflow over your helmet while maintaining clear forward vision.
  • Adjustable screens — Many touring bikes offer manually or electrically adjustable screens. These are ideal as you can raise the screen for motorway comfort and lower it for cooler ventilation on B-roads.
  • Spoiler extensions — A bolt-on spoiler adds 50-100mm to your existing screen without replacing it. Often the most cost-effective upgrade.

Screen Materials

Polycarbonate — Strong, lightweight, and scratch-resistant. The premium choice for touring screens. Brands like MRA and Puig use optical-grade polycarbonate for distortion-free viewing.

Acrylic (PMMA) — Cheaper but more brittle and prone to cracking. Adequate for budget applications but less durable than polycarbonate.

Tinted screens — Reduce glare in bright conditions but may reduce visibility at dawn and dusk. A clear screen is the safer all-round choice for touring.

Best Aftermarket Screens

MRA Touring Screen — The benchmark aftermarket touring screen available for most popular bikes. The spoiler lip at the top creates excellent turbulence reduction and the optical quality is superb.

Puig Touring Screen — Spanish-made screens with excellent wind protection and competitive pricing. Available in clear, light smoke, and dark smoke.

Givi Airflow — A mechanically adjustable screen that changes height at the touch of a lever while riding. Clever engineering at a reasonable price.

A windscreen upgrade is the single most effective comfort improvement for touring. If your standard screen leaves you battered by wind after an hour, a taller aftermarket screen will transform every mile of your tour into a more comfortable experience.

Troubleshooting Wind Buffeting

If your new screen creates helmet buffeting, try adjusting the angle by adding spacers behind the mounting points. A slight forward tilt often cures turbulence that a vertical screen creates. faq.q: How tall should my windscreen be?
faq.a: The screen top should be at chin or nose height in your riding position so airflow passes over your helmet while forward vision stays clear. If a screen is too short it hits you at chest or helmet height, creating more turbulence than no screen at all; too tall and you look through it in rain.

Polycarbonate is strong, lightweight and scratch-resistant, making it the premium touring choice, and brands like MRA and Puig use optical-grade polycarbonate for distortion-free viewing. Acrylic is cheaper but more brittle and prone to cracking, so it suits budget applications rather than serious touring.

faq.q: What is the cheapest way to improve wind protection?
faq.a: A bolt-on spoiler extension adds 50-100mm to your existing screen without replacing it, and is often the most cost-effective upgrade. If your bike has an adjustable screen, simply raise it for motorway comfort and lower it for cooler ventilation on B-roads before spending on a new one.

faq.q: My new screen causes helmet buffeting, what can I do?
faq.a: Try adjusting the angle by adding spacers behind the mounting points. A slight forward tilt often cures turbulence that a vertical screen creates. Every rider and bike combination differs, so some experimentation is normal, and a spoiler lip like the MRA touring screen's helps reduce buffeting.
